## What's new in 1.5.2

**Looks: how the pictures are drawn.** The screen saver can now draw the modules' pictures in more than one way. In the settings window, click **Look: Sharp pixels** at the end of the **Stretch to fit the screen** row (or press Alt+K) and pick from the menu:

- **Sharp pixels**, the default: the original, unaltered look, every pixel of the module's picture a crisp square block, the way Long After Dark has always drawn them.
- **CRT monitor**: the picture as a 1990s VGA monitor showed it, the kind of screen these modules were drawn for: a soft beam that melts dithering and softens jagged edges, faint scanlines, a fine mask and a little glow. It looks best on a 1440p or 4K monitor; on a 1080p one the scanlines are left out.
- **Curved CRT monitor**: the same, behind curved glass with rounded corners.
- **Smooth**: outlines redrawn as clean curves and diagonals instead of steps (Hyllian's Super-xBR), for flat cartoon art such as the Simpsons', the Looney Tunes', Disney's, The Far Side's and Dilbert's modules.
- **Shader preset**: a RetroArch shader preset (`.slangp`) of your own, drawn by librashader, which you download yourself: [Your own shader preset](https://github.com/starrlord/longafterdark/blob/v1.5.2/docs/INSTALL.md#your-own-shader-preset-advanced) says how.

**Ambient glow.** The menu's second group, **Bars**, can fill the bars beside a 4:3 module on a widescreen monitor (Intermission's, Star Wars', Star Trek's or Johnny Castaway) with a blurred, dimmed copy of its picture instead of black.

Nothing changes until you choose it: with **Sharp pixels** and **Black** bars, Long After Dark draws exactly as before. The other choices draw on your graphics card, through Direct3D 11, on every monitor, and in the `/window` for OBS too. **Preview** shows them; the settings window's small live preview shows the plain picture. If the graphics can't draw a look fast enough (Smooth on some integrated graphics, say), the screen saver goes back to sharp pixels on its own.
